# Sound

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Sound")`

Plays an audio file. Parented to a `BasePart`, the sound is positional: it gets quieter with distance and is heard from the side it is on. Parented to anything else, it plays at the same volume everywhere.

A positional sound is mixed to mono and panned left or right by its direction from the listener. Height is not conveyed, and a source directly ahead sounds the same as one directly behind. A sound that is not positional keeps its own stereo image.

A sound runs on simulation time. `TimePosition` advances by the tick length times `PlaybackSpeed` every tick, and `Ended` fires from that position. A replay reproduces both exactly, and a run with no audio device fires `Ended` on the same tick as a run with speakers. The length of the sound comes from its file.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Category` | `Enum.SoundCategory` | `Enum.SoundCategory.Effects` | read/write | The kind of sound: `Effects`, `Music` or `Voice`. It selects which of the player's volume settings applies (`AudioService.EffectsVolume`, `MusicVolume` or `VoiceVolume`). Music is automatically lowered while a voice plays. The category is replicated with the sound, unlike `Group`, which is local to each machine. |
| `Content` | `Content` | `""` | read/write | The audio file, as an `asset://` path. WAV, MP3, FLAC and Ogg Vorbis are supported. A file of up to ten seconds is decoded once and kept in memory. A longer file is streamed, so a long music track uses about as much memory as the size of its file.<br><br>The length of the sound is the length of the file, and `Ended` fires when `TimePosition` reaches it.<br><br>A path to a file that does not exist plays a one-second placeholder tone instead of silence, so that a missing file is noticed. `DebugService:GetStat("AudioClipsMissing")` returns how many sounds are missing their file. |
| `Group` | `AudioGroup?` | `nil` | read/write | The `AudioGroup` whose volume this sound's volume is multiplied by, or nil for none. |
| `Looped` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the sound starts again when it reaches the end. A looped sound never fires `Ended`. |
| `Loudness` | `number` | — | read-only | How loud the recording is at the current moment on this machine, from 0 to 1. It is the level of the recording over about the last twentieth of a second at `TimePosition`; a full-scale tone reads 1. Use it to open a character's mouth while a line plays.<br><br>It is the level of the recording itself. No volume setting and no distance affects it. It is measured on the language this machine plays, so it differs between machines; do not use it in game rules. It is 0 while the sound is not playing, during the silence after a shorter language, and for a sound with no file. |
| `PlaybackSpeed` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How fast the sound plays, which also changes its pitch. 2 is an octave higher and half as long. It must be greater than 0; use `Playing` to pause. |
| `Playing` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the sound is advancing. Setting it resumes or pauses the sound at `TimePosition`; it never rewinds. Use `Play` to start from the beginning and `Stop` to stop and rewind. |
| `RollOffMaxDistance` | `number` | `80` | read/write | The distance from the listener at which a positional sound becomes silent, in meters. Between `RollOffMinDistance` and this distance, the volume falls off linearly. |
| `RollOffMinDistance` | `number` | `8` | read/write | The distance from the listener within which a positional sound plays at its full `Volume`, in meters. Beyond it the sound gets quieter. A sound that is not positional ignores it. |
| `TimeLength` | `number` | — | read-only | The length of `Content`, in seconds. It is the length of the file, or one second for the placeholder tone of a missing file. It is 0 until the length has been read, which happens on the first tick after `Content` is set.<br><br>A sound recorded in several languages is as long as its longest recording. The value is the same on every machine whatever language each one plays, so `Ended` fires on the same tick everywhere. A shorter recording is followed by silence. A sound with a `Caption` and no file in any language lasts as long as its caption is shown. |
| `TimePosition` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The current position in the sound, in seconds, from 0 to `TimeLength`. Set it to seek. A value below 0 raises an error. A value beyond the end is clamped to the end, or wrapped if the sound is `Looped`. |
| `Volume` | `number` | `0.5` | read/write | A multiplier on the loudness of the sound, combined with its group's volume and with the falloff over distance. The default is 0.5, which leaves headroom when several sounds play at once. |

## Methods

### `GetBands(): (number, number, number)`

Returns the level that `Loudness` measures, split into three frequency bands, each from 0 to 1. The bands are low (80 to 500 Hz), middle (500 to 2,500 Hz) and high (2,500 to 10,000 Hz). A full-scale tone inside one band reads 1 in that band and 0 in the others. Use it to tell an open mouth from a wide or a round one, or to drive a visualizer.

The bands are computed only when requested, and once per tick however many times they are requested. Like `Loudness`, the result differs between machines.

### `Pause()`

Stops the sound at its current position. `Resume` continues from there, and `Play` starts again from the beginning. It is the same as setting `Playing` to false.

### `Play()`

Plays the sound from the start, or from `TimePosition` if a script set it since the sound last started. Calling it on a sound that is already playing restarts it. To continue after `Pause`, use `Resume`.

The language of the sound is chosen when it starts. `Content` is looked for under `l10n/<VoiceLocale>/`, then under the language without its region, then at the path as written. A sound that is playing finishes in the language it started in.

### `Resume()`

Continues the sound from `TimePosition`, where `Pause` left it. It is the same as setting `Playing` to true.

### `Stop()`

Stops the sound and rewinds it to the start. `Ended` does not fire.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Ended()`

Fires on the tick a sound that is not `Looped` reaches its end. The sound stops and `TimePosition` returns to 0. It fires on the same tick in a replay, in a headless run and on every machine.

### `Loaded()`

Fires when the sound's `Content` is ready to play. It currently fires immediately.
